event.name: 25 October 2018 Mw 6.8 Zakynthos earthquake (Ionian Sea, Greece)
event.tectonic_setting: Transition between Cephalonia Transform Fault Zone and western Hellenic Arc subduction zone
event.region: Offshore southwest Zakynthos, Ionian Sea, Greece

reference.title: The 2018 Mw 6.8 Zakynthos (Ionian Sea, Greece) earthquake: seismic source and local tsunami characterization
reference.digitized_figure: Figure 4a, upper panel (journal p. 1050, uploaded PDF p. 8)

inversion.method: Two-stage non-linear joint kinematic inversion using simulated annealing followed by statistical analysis of an ensemble of nearly 250,000 good-fitting models. At the original fault-plane nodes, the inversion solves peak slip velocity, rise time, rake and rupture time. Inversion model is ensemble-average preferred NP1 plane.
inversion.green_function_model: Discrete wavenumber / finite-element Green functions computed using local 1-D crustal velocity model (Haslinger et al. 1999).
inversion.notes: FIGURE-DIGITIZED SLIP ESTIMATES, NOT AUTHOR-RELEASED INVERSION VALUES. This file digitizes TOTAL SLIP colors ONLY from Figure 4(a), upper panel, not the LOWER rise-time panel and not the kinematic slip-velocity snapshots. Black contour lines in the upper panel are RUPTURE-TIME contours at 1-s intervals, NOT slip contours. Black arrows are slip vectors and the red star marks nucleation: these three overlays were excluded from slip-color sampling. Preferred fault geometry: USGS NP1 strike 9°, dip 39° ESE, rake 167° (Table 1). The figure horizontal axis increases SSW to NNE, with plotted -36..+27 km relative to the hypocentral along-strike origin; output along_strike_km is measured from the SSW edge (plot -36km), NOT the plotted signed coordinate. Vertical axis uses absolute down-dip DISTANCE, here 0..45 km positive downward; negative tick labels in the figure indicate position down the fault, not negative physical depth. Depth_km is computed as down_dip_km*sin(39°), matching the right-hand approximate depth axis, and is NOT a separately inverted depth. The 42×30, 1.5km output grid is a chosen sampling of the smoothed published image, while Cirella et al. specify the ORIGINAL INVERSION NODES are spaced 4.5km in both directions; never treat the 1.5km grid as their inversion mesh. Printed 0..1.8m color scale has approximately 0.15m bands; cells are represented by approximate color-bin midpoints (0.225 to 1.725m), rather than implying 1-mm precision. White/background/pixel areas with no recoverable positive-slip color are assigned 0, NOT proved exactly zero. Contours and arrows obscure parts of both slip regions, so enclosed gaps were filled conservatively from adjacent colors. Reported peak 1.8m and minor asperity ~1.0m are paper values; reconstructed peaks can differ. Single nominal average rake 167° is assigned in every output patch for schema compatibility, but the paper inverted spatially VARYING rake and described an increasing reverse component at depth; these 167° cells are not published patch-specific rakes. Individual patch latitude/longitude null because the image does not establish an exact georeferenced upper-left plane corner; hypocenter coordinates below are an independent source observation, not that corner. The 63×45km plotted domain is inferred from the axes, not a claim that all of it slipped. Image-derived spatial resolution, depth assumptions and reconstructed moment are not independently validated. Original detailed faulting_style description: dominantly right-lateral strike-slip, minor reverse component. Digitization variant descriptor: figure4a_total_slip_colorbar_calibrated_1p5km_image_digitization.
